note: Lines for the three plot warnings. Invention. 'whispers', 'rumors' and 'named' are the stock lines used when the switch 'Warnings are clues' is off. 'clues' are used when it is on: each tells of one thing the plotters really did. 'far' lines are for Whispers and give no faction; 'near' lines are for Rumors and Named. {grudge} is the grievance of the man concerned, {faction} his faction, {target} a man who was approached and said no.
whispers: A toast at dinner goes undrunk.
A guest leaves your table early, without a word.
Two men fall silent when your steward passes.
Someone has been asking which nights you sleep at the dockyards.
A slave is seen carrying letters out by the Achradina gate.
rumors: Men say {faction} are meeting at night.
Your friends hear that {faction} have money moving.
In the market they say {faction} have had enough of you.
named: Your informers bring you a name: {names}.
The name on every tongue is {names}.

far: Someone who says {grudge} has begun to meet men after dark.
A man who cannot forget that {grudge} has been asking who else feels the same.
Your steward hears of a grievance aired too freely at a dinner: {grudge}.
near: A man of {faction} who says {grudge} is gathering friends.
Among {faction}, someone who says {grudge} has stopped complaining and started counting heads.

far: A second man with a grievance has been seen at the same door. His complaint: {grudge}.
Someone new keeps the late hours of the others. He is heard to say {grudge}.
near: A man of {faction} has joined them. His complaint is that {grudge}.
Someone from {faction} who says {grudge} has thrown in with them.

far: {target} tells your steward he was sounded out against you, and said no. He will not say by whom.
{target} was approached by someone who wanted him against you. He refused, and now he is afraid.
near: {target} says a man of {faction} sounded him out against you. He said no.
{target} came to your door: someone among {faction} tried to win him over, and failed.

far: Someone is paying the debts of men who hate you.
Money is moving to men who have no reason to love you.
near: Silver from {faction} is reaching men with grievances against you.

far: Your mercenaries have new silver, and it isn't yours.
near: Your mercenaries have new silver, and it isn't yours. The captain will not meet your eye.

far: Someone has been buying swords in Achradina, a few at a time.
near: Someone of {faction} has been buying swords in Achradina, a few at a time.

far: Nothing new is heard, but the talk has not stopped.
The same unease at dinner. No one says why.
Your steward has nothing new, only a feeling.
Doors that were open at night are shut now.
A servant you trust asks for a day's leave, and will not say why.
Your cook says the market has gone quiet when your name comes up.
Someone has been reading the letters on your desk, or you think so.
near: Nothing new this season. The same men still meet.
The talk goes quiet when your people come near. They are waiting for something.
No new names, but no one has left them either.
The same houses keep their lamps lit late.
Your watchers see the same faces at the same doors.
Nothing you can prove, and nothing that has stopped.
